title: Loneliness, US students, 1978-2011
next_action: Obtain Clark et al. supplementary/author data and recover the MTF public-use item files and codebooks needed to reproduce the six-item triennial high-school series.
notes: The paper and official MTF distribution route are resolved. The figure combines a 48-sample Revised UCLA college meta-analysis with a six-item MTF high-school series on separate half-standard-deviation axes. No plotted values were digitized and no proxy reconstruction was drawn.
book_citation: Clark, Loxton, & Tobin 2015. College students (left axis): Revised UCLA Loneliness Scale, trend line across many samples, taken from their fig. 1. High school students (right axis): Mean rating of six loneliness items from the Monitoring the Future survey, triennial means, taken from their fig. 4.

status_evidence.basis: exact cited paper and official MTF source family identified; both numeric components not yet recovered
source_chain: Clark, Loxton, and Tobin (2015), Figures 1 and 4
Monitoring the Future six loneliness items
status_evidence.blocker: Publisher supplementary files returned HTTP 403 and the exact college data are not exposed in the accessible record. MTF files are public but the six-item form/grade harmonization and triennial aggregation are not yet reconstructed.

issues: No book-period comparison can be generated

extension.notes: Do not add a successor loneliness series until the two book-period source components are reconstructed.

research.claim_summary: Loneliness trends decline among US college students and among 8th-, 10th-, and 12th-grade students over the periods shown, with the two source series normalized to comparable slopes but not comparable absolute heights.
research.original_dataset: Clark et al. (2015) college cross-temporal meta-analysis and Monitoring the Future repeated cross-sectional survey data for six loneliness items.
research.confidence_score: high for source chain; low for numeric recovery

reference.source_note_ocr: Clark, Loxton, & Tobin 2015. College students (left axis): Revised UCLA Loneliness Scale, trend line across many samples, taken from their fig. 1. High school students (right axis): Mean rating of six loneliness items from the Monitoring the Future survey, triennial means, taken from their fig. 4. Each axis spans half a standard deviation, so the slopes of the college and high school curves are commensurable, but their relative heights are not.
